message.content: In lions, one of the most well‑known dominant genetic traits is the development of a mane in adult male individuals. The presence of a mane is controlled by a dominant allele at the *ASIP* locus (agouti signaling protein), which regulates melanin production and leads to the characteristic dark fur around the head and neck. This allele masks the recessive allele that would otherwise produce a maneless phenotype.
